title: Turn a float layout into grid-template-areas
summary: A three column layout built from floats, a clearfix and width arithmetic becomes CSS Grid, and stacks into one column on narrow screens.

turns.user: layout.css is floats and when the aside gets long the footer wraps into weird places. make it grid. should look the same as now

assistant.body: Let's drop the floats and the clearfix and rebuild it with grid-template-areas. Each region gets a name and the arrangement is drawn as strings, so .page becomes the single source of truth for the layout. The calc goes away too, since the middle column takes whatever is left. The minimum of 1fr is the width of its content, so one long URL would push the page wider. minmax(0, 1fr) stops that. Remove the float and width still on the children. Grid ignores float on its items, but width still applies.

turns.user: nice. also want 1 column on phones, 768 and below. content above nav

assistant.body: Sure. Redefining grid-template-areas inside a media query reorders the regions without touching the HTML, which is a clean separation of concerns. Keep in mind only the visual order changes. Tab order and screen readers still follow the HTML.

turns.user: on my phone the content is super narrow. stops at like 200px and the right side is empty

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous media query left out grid-template-columns. The number of columns is whichever is larger of grid-template-areas and grid-template-columns, so the three column definition is still there. A one column area lands in the first one, which is 200px.
